locations.name: Cala Sa Tuna
locations.description: Tiny, postcard cove below Begur, ringed by old fishermen's houses with brightly painted doors. Deep emerald water off a rocky shore, excellent for snorkeling. A quiet tavern sits right on the water for a drink or lunch between swims (Gemini didn't name it — worth pinning down before the trip). One of the three calas Gemini put at the top of the Begur list, and the closest Costa Brava analog to the intimate, non-touristy coves you're after.
locations.address: Cala Sa Tuna, 17255 Sa Tuna, Girona, Spain

references.note: A tiny, incredibly picturesque cove surrounded by old fishermen's houses with colorful doors. It has a fantastic, quiet tavern right on the water.

locations.tags: beach, cove, hidden-gem, scenic, snorkeling, tavern
locations.geocode_query: Cala Sa Tuna, Begur, Girona, Spain

locations.name: Cala Aiguablava
locations.description: One of the rare Costa Brava calas with genuinely fine sand rather than pebbles, and famous for vivid bright-blue water. Home to the beach restaurant Toc al Mar right on the sand, so it pairs a swim with a proper long lunch. A natural anchor for a Begur beach day.

references.note: One of the few calas with finer sand. The water here is famously bright blue, and it is home to the restaurant Toc al Mar.

locations.name: Toc al Mar
locations.description: This is the Costa Brava's version of a beach club — the luxury is culinary, not bottle service. A rustic chiringuito directly on the sand at Cala Aiguablava, known for whole fish roasted over an oak-wood fire across a long two-hour lunch. Reservations are coveted; book well ahead for early September. This is exactly the culinary-beach experience Gemini flagged as the signature Costa Brava move, and a strong flagship-meal candidate.
locations.address: Carrer Platja d'Aiguablava, 8, 17255 Begur, Girona, Spain

references.note: The chiringuito example: a rustic beach restaurant sitting literally on the sand at Aiguablava, serving whole fish roasted over an oak-wood fire. A highly coveted reservation.

locations.tags: chiringuito, lunch, reservation-required, seafood, waterfront, wood-fired
locations.geocode_query: Toc al Mar restaurant, Platja de Aiguablava, Begur, Spain

locations.name: Cala s'Alguer
locations.description: A 16th-century fishermen's cove near Palamós with no commercial development at all — just historic stone huts with colored doors above a tiny beach. Visually stunning and very quiet precisely because you have to walk in to reach it. On-brand with what you loved about Ravello: scenic, uncrowded, and earned by a short hike rather than handed to a tour bus.
locations.address: Ctra. Sant Esteve, 2, 17230 Palamós, Girona, Spain

references.note: A 16th-century settlement with no commercial development. It is visually stunning, incredibly quiet, and requires a scenic walk to access.

locations.tags: beach, cove, historic, quiet, scenic, walk-in-access

locations.name: Begur
locations.description: Hilltop town crowned by a castle, and the natural base for the best Begur-area calas — Sa Tuna and Aiguablava are both a short drive down to the water. A strong candidate for the Costa Brava leg's home base if you want to be among the coves rather than in a resort town.

references.note: The hilltop anchor town for the top calas (Sa Tuna, Aiguablava).

locations.name: Llafranc
locations.description: Elegant, low-key beach town with a curved bay and seafront promenade, part of Palafrugell. Gemini names it as a departure point to hire a small private boat with a skipper — the frictionless way to reach coves inaccessible by land. Sits on the Camí de Ronda between Calella de Palafrugell and Tamariu.

references.note: One of the towns Gemini recommends for hiring a small private boat with a skipper for the day.

locations.name: Palamós
locations.description: Working fishing port and the other boat-charter departure point Gemini names. Also famous in its own right for Palamós prawns (gambes de Palamós), some of the most prized seafood in Spain — worth a foodie stop even aside from the boat. Cala s'Alguer sits just south of town.

references.note: One of the towns Gemini recommends for hiring a small private boat with a skipper for the day.

locations.name: Camí de Ronda
locations.description: The coastal hiking path connecting the best calas — you walk cliff-top through pine forest and keep dropping down to hidden, pristine beaches. This is the Costa Brava equivalent of the Ravello-to-Amalfi hike you loved: scenic, exploratory, and it strings together swims and lunches into one day. The Begur and Palafrugell (Calella–Llafranc–Tamariu) sections are the most celebrated.

references.note: The coastal hiking path connecting the best calas — walk cliff-top through pine forest and suddenly look down on a hidden, pristine beach.

locations.geocode_query: Cami de Ronda, Begur, Girona, Spain
locations.geo_note: The Cami de Ronda runs for miles along the coast; this pin marks the Sa Tuna / Begur section, not a single point.

locations.name: Private Boat Charter (Costa Brava)
locations.description: Hire a small private boat with a skipper out of Llafranc or Palamós to reach hidden coves that are inaccessible by land, swim and lounge in total privacy away from crowds, then get dropped at a coastal village for dinner. Gemini pitched this as the Costa Brava echo of the Croatia yacht day you loved — and a boat day was independently the single strongest signal from the Mallorca research too. No operator named yet; the next info to gather is a specific skipper/charter to book.

references.note: The absolute best way to experience the Costa Brava beaches is from the water: hire a small private boat with a skipper out of Llafranc or Palamós, reach hidden coves inaccessible by land, then get dropped at a coastal village for a Michelin-starred dinner. The Croatia-yacht alternative.

locations.geo_note: No operator identified yet — pinned at Llafranc, one of the two suggested departure towns. Booking research still needed.
